newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 30.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- The chairman of the task group on insider trading, Mervyn King, has been accused of riding roughshod over the contrary views of several group members by presenting a report recommending that insider trading be criminalised.

- The public service faces disruptions from Tuesday which could culminate in national strike action as four Congress of South African Trade Unions public sector unions begin a campaign to challenge the government's final pay offer for teachers, police and other employees.

- Expectations of at least one interest rate cut within the next few months were heightened last week after the Reserve Bank released figures showing a slowdown in the growth of money supply and private credit extension.

- The Building Industries' Federation of South Africa is set to go head to head with the government over a draft bill which will give statutory recognition to the National Homebuilders' Registration Council.

- Northern Province Premier Ngoako Ramatlhodi was certain to reshuffle his cabinet this week as he attempted to impress his authority on the legislature and the African National Congress in the province, top sources said.
BUSINESS REPORT

- South Africa's economy shed 71,000 jobs in the non-agricultural formal sector last year, shattering the government's hopes of creating 126,000 jobs, according to figures from the Central Statistical Service.
- For the first time in three months, the money supply and credit extension growth figures moved in the same direction when they dropped from April to May.
- The Southern Sun hotel group has built a 26 million rand centralised production kitchen in Midrand that will eventually provide prepared, vacuum-packed food for most of the hotels in the group.

- The Industrial Development Corp has committed 1.7 billion rand to a wide range of agricultural beneficiation projects as part of a broader programme to boost the country's competitive edge in agro-industries, corporation deputy general manager Johann Kriek said.
- Japanese tyre company Bridgestone has approved a 220 million rand investment in its South African operations, the group said.
SAKE-BEELD
- The American Chambers of Commerce in South Africa, grouping around 250 U.S.-based firms doing business in South Africa, has slammed the high levels of crime in the country.

- Mali gold mining company Societe Miniere de Loulo (Somilo) approved a majority shareholding bought by Randgold Resources Ltd, the African gold mining and exploration arm of Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd.
- The competition board is to probe the affairs of South African Breweries and the KWV wine cooperative.

- Anglo American Coal Corp Ltd and sister company Minorco SA had reached agreement in principle with unlisted commodity group Glencore International AG and Rio Tinto Plc to form a coal joint venture in Colombia.
- Financial services giant Sanlam has welcomed the relaxation of exchange controls, but says it will make the choices in investment opportunities much more complicated.
THE CITIZEN
- Bitterly cold weather conditions will hit large parts of the country with most maximum temperatures in the interior expected to fall as a result of a cold front which moved over the area on Sunday.

- President Nelson Mandela and Welfare Minister Geraldine Fraser-Moleketi are soon to visit the flood-ravaged Cape Peninsula, where about 4,500 people have been left homeless by storms which lashed the region.
